core.big_idea: The exalted Jesus is proclaimed, people respond, and a Spirit-formed community becomes visible.

passages.reading_note: Read the central passage in context; select age-appropriate portions when needed.

core.metanarrative_position: Apostolic mission: The exalted Jesus is proclaimed, people respond, and a Spirit-formed community becomes visible.

claims.statement: Peter proclaims Jesus’ death, resurrection, exaltation, and lordship.
Peter tells hearers to repent and be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ.
Those who received the word were baptized and added to the community.
The community devoted itself to apostolic teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayers.
The curriculum treats Acts 2 as a major conversion and church-formation text while still reading narrative details with attention to what is descriptive and what is normative.
claims.prohibited_overstatement: Do not state this claim more strongly than its evidence classification allows.
claims.interpretive_hinge: The distinction between what a narrative describes and what it establishes as normative for later practice.

core.interpretation_skill: Observe text; reconstruct context; account for genre; distinguish text, canonical synthesis, inference, historical context, and application.

learning.foundation_objective: Analyse Acts 2:14-47 and explain the case that the exalted Jesus is proclaimed, people respond, and a Spirit-formed community becomes visible.
learning.extension_objective: Test the claim against context, genre, canonical synthesis, credible alternatives, and the limits of the available evidence.
know: The exalted Jesus is proclaimed, people respond, and a Spirit-formed community becomes visible.
The lesson belongs within the wider biblical storyline.
understand: Meaning depends on context and genre.
Application should follow what the text supports rather than replace it.
practise: State one observation before giving an interpretation.
Read Acts 2:37-42 and identify what is commanded, what happens in the narrative, and what ongoing practices are described.
become: A learner who reads Scripture carefully and responds with trust, wisdom, and love.
success_evidence: Student can summarize the central passage.
Student can state the big idea without unsupported details.
Student can distinguish at least one observation from one application.

zero_prep_card.objective: Analyse Acts 2:14-47 and explain the case that the exalted Jesus is proclaimed, people respond, and a Spirit-formed community becomes visible.
zero_prep_card.opening: Ask: What do you notice first in this passage before we explain what it means?
say: Peter proclaims Jesus’ death, resurrection, exaltation, and lordship.
Peter tells hearers to repent and be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ.
Those who received the word were baptized and added to the community.
The exalted Jesus is proclaimed, people respond, and a Spirit-formed community becomes visible.
ask: What happens or is said in the passage?
What does this show about Jesus, God, people, or the biblical story?
Which statement is directly in the text?
What is one careful response for us?
zero_prep_card.do: Complete the Acts 2 Observation, Pattern, and Inference Grid activity.
zero_prep_card.close: Pray using one truth from the passage and one faithful response.

preparation.passage_context: Apostolic mission: The exalted Jesus is proclaimed, people respond, and a Spirit-formed community becomes visible.
text_observations: Peter proclaims Jesus’ death, resurrection, exaltation, and lordship.
Peter tells hearers to repent and be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ.
Those who received the word were baptized and added to the community.
The community devoted itself to apostolic teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayers.
interpretation_notes: Start with the principal passage before moving to broader synthesis.
Keep genre, original audience, and immediate context visible.
Label synthesis, inference, historical context, and application rather than presenting them as quotations.
theological_guardrails: Do not pressure students to be baptized during a classroom lesson.
Do not turn Acts 2 into a mechanical checklist detached from faith, repentance, Christ, and continuing discipleship.
Distinguish Pentecost’s unique signs from ordinary Christian experience today.

likely_questions.question: Does Acts 2 teach baptism is part of conversion?
likely_questions.purpose: Within this curriculum, Acts 2 is read alongside other conversion passages as presenting baptism as integral to the gospel response, not an optional symbol after salvation.

likely_questions.question: Should every church copy every detail of Acts 2:42-47 literally?
likely_questions.purpose: Some practices are clearly central; other narrative details require careful reasoning about context, pattern, and normative force.

family.title: Pentecost and the Church
family.parent_intro: Use the passage itself first. Keep the conversation concrete, honest, and free from pressure.

flow.instructions: Ask one simple question that links the theme to ordinary life.
Read selected portions of Acts 2:14-47. Ask what everyone notices.
Say the big idea in your own words: The exalted Jesus is proclaimed, people respond, and a Spirit-formed community becomes visible.
Use the Acts 2 Observation, Pattern, and Inference Grid idea verbally or on paper.

quiz.question: What is the principal passage for Pentecost and the Church?
quiz.explanation: The lesson is governed by its principal passage.

quiz.question: Which comes first in careful Bible reading?
quiz.explanation: Observe what the text says before moving to interpretation or application.

quiz.question: Peter proclaims Jesus’ death, resurrection, exaltation, and lordship.
quiz.explanation: This statement is directly supported by the principal passage.

quiz.question: Should an interpretation be presented as a quotation from the text when the text does not directly say it?
quiz.explanation: Interpretation and inference should be labelled honestly.

accessibility.reading_level: Teen reading with explicit interpretive scaffolding
accessibility.plain_language_rule: Define unfamiliar terms from the passage before using theological shorthand.
neurodiversity_supports: Offer verbal or written response options.
Allow students to pass on personal-sharing questions.
non_reader_support: Read the passage aloud and use icons, sequence cards, or oral choices.

do_not_ask: Do not require disclosure of trauma, family finances, grief, or private spiritual decisions.
Do not pressure a child or young person toward baptism or another public response.
safeguarding.teacher_response: Answer from the passage, acknowledge uncertainty where needed, and route personal or safety concerns to appropriate adults rather than solving them in class.
